name: EAGLE: Speculative Sampling Requires Rethinking Feature Uncertainty
problem: Token-level speculative drafting has irreducible uncertainty that caps acceptance rate; the draft model is forced to guess the next token in the same way the target does.
mechanism: Draft in FEATURE space instead of token space. An autoregressive feature-level draft model (a single transformer layer) predicts the target's SECOND-TO-TOP-LAYER hidden feature sequence. The predicted feature is then fed through the target's frozen lm_head to yield a draft token. The key move for handling feature-level uncertainty: shift the input sequence by one time step - feed [feat_1, ..., feat_t, embed_t] rather than [embed_1, ..., embed_t] - so the draft head sees the previous token's embedding and can resolve the uncertainty the authors identify. Draft head is tiny (~one decoder layer).
speedup_reported: For LLaMA2-Chat 70B, latency speedup 2.7x-3.5x AND doubled throughput, while maintaining the exact generated-text distribution. Evaluated across the Vicuna and LLaMA2-Chat series plus Mixtral 8x7B Instruct, on dialogue, code generation, math reasoning, and instruction following. The 70B figure is a 70B target with a one-layer draft head - the draft/target size ratio is extreme, which is the point of the paper.
notes:
ADOPTION, precisely: this is the best-engine-supported of the recent draft-model variants. vLLM ships EAGLE and EAGLE-3 as speculative methods, SGLang ships EAGLE-3, and llama.cpp has an EAGLE path; the EAGLE-3 headline throughput number is measured inside SGLang, which is itself evidence of upstream support rather than a bespoke harness. Weights are released so it is deployable without retraining the target. VENUE NOTE: Semantic Scholar gives no venue for 2401.15077 and the arXiv comment field carries none, so venue = arxiv-preprint, year = arXiv v1 (Jan 2024). Note the distinction from Medusa, also a multi-head method: Medusa predicts TOKENS from the backbone hidden state, EAGLE autoregresses over FEATURES and reuses the target's lm_head - which is why EAGLE's acceptance rate is higher and why the two are not interchangeable in a benchmark table.
